20.04.2023 WPMB No. 34 of 2023
Hon’ble Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
1. Mr. Shobhit Saharia and Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, 
learned counsels for the petitioner. 
2. Issue notice.
3. Mr. Vikas Pande, learned Standing counsel for 
the State of Uttarakhand, appears and accepts notice 
on behalf of respondent nos. 1 and 2.
4. Mr. Siddhartha Jain, learned counsel appears and 
accepts notice on behalf of respondent no. 4.
5. Let notice issue to respondent nos. 3, 5, 6 & 7, 
returnable on 18.09.2023, by all permitted modes, 
including electronically. 
6. The respondent-authorities should file their 
counter affidavit within six weeks. In the counter 
affidavit, it should specifically be stated, whether or not
a final report in relation to the liquidation of the Society 
in question, has been passed, and, if so, the same 
should be placed on record. 
7. Rejoinder before the next date. 
8. List on 18.09.2023.
9. In the meantime, the respondents, to whom land 
has been allotted, shall maintain status quo, with 
regard to the title and condition of the land.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
 20.04.2023 20.04.2023
Rahul

 Mr. Shobhit Saharia, learned counsel for the 
petitioner, Mr. Mohindar Singh Bisht, learned Brief 
Holder for the State / respondent Nos. 1 and 2, and 
Mr. B.M. Pingal, learned counsel for respondent No. 
4. 
2. Counsel for the petitioner has referred to 
Section 74B of the Uttarakhand Cooperative 
Societies Act, whereby any surplus assets as shown 
in the final report of the liquidator of a society 
which has been wound up can be divided and in the 
present case, no final report of the liquidator has 
been given. 
3. Counsel for the State, on the basis of 
affidavit filed on 8th January, 2024, has referred to 
the letter dated 17th July, 2020 to be a final report. 
4. Counsel for the petitioner states that this 
letter itself shows that there is no final report.  5. List this matter on 11th June, 2024. 
6. Interim order to continue. 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J) (Ritu Bahri, CJ)
